# @liberation-data/desk

A desktop for the web, in React: windows that fill the desk, layered, and arrange when asked, with a dock, a menu bar,
commands routed to whoever is responsible, and the controls to fill the windows. Apache-2.0.

This file is the whole public surface in one place, for a coding agent. Prose for people:
`docs/guide.md`. How it should look and behave: `HIG.md`.

## Install and entry points

```
npm install @liberation-data/desk        # peer: react ^19
```

```ts
import { createDesk }                    from '@liberation-data/desk'        // no DOM, no React
import { Desktop, DeskProvider }         from '@liberation-data/desk/react'  // components and hooks
import { createFx }                      from '@liberation-data/desk/fx'     // sounds; opt-in, no React
import '@liberation-data/desk/desk.css'                                      // tokens and styles
// or only the parts you draw: css/tokens.css (required) + windows|dock|menus|controls|overlays|
// conversation|search|setup|apps.css, then looks.css last
```

## The shape of an app

```tsx
const desk = createDesk()

<DeskShell desk={desk} look={look}>  {/* desk + bus + toasts; or DeskProvider on its own */}
      <MenuBar menus={…} status={…} />
      <div className="screen">  {/* position: relative; the stage fills it */}
        <Desktop title={id => TITLES[id]} renderWindow={id => SURFACES[id]} empty={…} />
        <InputBar onSubmit={…} />
        <Dock entries={…} side="left" />  {/* a sibling of Desktop, so it makes its own room */}
        <SearchPalette open={…} onOpenChange={…} search={…} />
      </div>
</DeskShell>
```

Rules that are easy to get wrong:
- `.desk-stage` fills its parent: give the parent a height, and `position: relative` if the dock or input
  bar overlays it. An overlay `<Dock>` beside the `<Desktop>` (same parent) makes its own room; set
  `--desk-inset-bottom` only for something else of the app's overlaying the bottom — never for the dock.
- The look (`look?: 'auto' | 'mac' | 'gnome' | 'windows'` on DeskShell/DeskProvider, default `auto` = the
  device's) is chrome only: it never changes tokens like `--desk-accent`, and never the keyboard — shortcuts
  follow the device. The app stores a user's choice and passes it back. `useLook()` returns the resolved look
  for chrome the app draws itself, e.g. a Window menu: Zoom on `mac`, Maximize elsewhere.
- A window is an id; `renderWindow(id)` says what it looks like. Every open window renders, including ones
  offstage in the touch layout — that is what preserves their state.
- Opening a window that is already open focuses it. For a second window onto the same thing use
  `openInstance`, and render by `windowType(id)`.

## Core: `@liberation-data/desk`

```ts
createDesk(options?: DeskOptions): Desk
interface DeskOptions { cascade?: Partial<CascadeOptions>; stage?: () => Size; initial?: DeskState; layouts?: LayoutStore }
// layouts: remembers each window type's last mode/frame (saved by float/fill/zoom, not placeAll or open frames);
// open() without mode/frame restores it, fitted to the stage (fills if too small); more instances step +x,+y.
localLayoutStore(key): LayoutStore   // localStorage 'desk.layouts.<key>'
interface LayoutStore { load(type): SavedLayout | undefined; save(type, layout: SavedLayout): void }
fitFrame(frame, stage, min?): Frame | null; stepFrom(frame, open: Frame[], stage, step, margin): Frame

interface Desk {
  getState(): DeskState
  subscribe(listener: (state: DeskState) => void): () => void
  open(id: string, options?: { mode?: 'filled' | 'floating'; frame?: Frame }): void   // default fills; a frame floats
  openInstance(type: string, options?): string    // 'query', then 'query#2' — returns the id it opened
  close(id: string): void
  closeAll(): void
  minimize(id: string): void                      // off the desk, still open and loaded; see Minimizing
  focus(id: string): void                         // forward, and back onto the desk when minimized
  float(id: string, frame?: Frame): void          // no frame: last place it sat, else the next cascade step
  fill(id: string): void                          // fill the desk; remembers the frame for float()
  toggleMode(id: string): void                    // zoom: fill ⇄ free
  placeAll(frames: Record<string, Frame>): void   // free windows at these frames; Arrange uses it
  fitToStage(): FitResult                         // the desk resized: bring windows back on, restore
                                                  // them when the room returns; <Desktop> calls it
  // FitResult { moved, squeezed, restored }: >1 squeezed means the layout is gone, and <Desktop>
  // then arranges for the screen there is now. Frames from the bigger screen still come back.
  restore(state: DeskState): void                 // e.g. from a URL; normalised, not trusted
  setStage(stage: () => Size): void
}

interface DeskState {
  windows: readonly DeskWindow[]   // the order they were opened = the order Arrange lays out
  stack: readonly string[]         // back to front; the last one NOT minimized is key
  minimized?: readonly string[]    // open and off the desk; absent while nothing is
}
type DeskWindow = { id: string; mode: 'filled' } | { id: string; mode: 'floating'; frame: Frame }
interface Frame { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }

focusedId(state): string | null
windowType(id): string                            // 'query#2' → 'query'; what to render
instancesOf(state, type): DeskWindow[]            // every window of a kind
isOpen(state, id): boolean
normalise(state): DeskState
cascadeFrame(slot, stage, options?): Frame
cascadeSlot(frame, stage, options?): number
nextCascadeFrame(windows, stage, options?): Frame
EMPTY: DeskState
```

Every window opens filled, layered over the others; a filled window follows the stage's size. Arrange
lays windows out once as free windows (`placeAll`); moving or resizing one changes only that one. Dragging a
filled window frees it where it sits. Edge drops take a half; double-click or the green control zooms. State is immutable; every mutator returns void and notifies
subscribers only when something actually changed.

### Minimizing

```ts
desk.minimize(id)                     // off the desk, still open and still mounted
desk.focus(id) / desk.open(id)        // and back, to the mode and frame it had — there is no un-minimize
isMinimized(state, id) / onDesk(state)
state.minimized?: readonly WindowId[] // absent while nothing is minimized
```

Deliberately NOT a `WindowMode`: the window keeps its mode and frame, which is how it comes back to them.
`focusedId` skips minimized windows, so a desk with everything minimized has no key window and shows
`<Desktop empty>`; Arrange, window cycling and `fitToStage` skip them too. The title bar's amber control and
`DeskCommands.minimizeWindow` (⌘M) do it. The dock keeps `data-running` and adds `data-minimized`;
`windowMenuItems` gives the item `detail: 'Minimized'`.

### URL and history

```ts
syncWithLocation(desk, stage: () => Size, options?: LocationOptions, env?: LocationEnv): () => void
serialize(state, options?): URLSearchParams        // #w=rides,map~_&f=rides  (`~` = free, `_` = minimized)
parse(params, stage, options?): DeskState
interface LocationOptions { key?: 'w'; focusKey?: 'f'; isKnown?: (id: string) => boolean }
```

Opening or closing pushes history (Back closes); focus and mode changes replace it. Frames are never in the
URL. Other hash parameters are left alone. A URL naming no windows adopts whatever the app opened.

### The browser tab

```tsx
useDocumentTitle(title: (id: WindowId) => string, options?: DocumentTitleOptions): void
interface DocumentTitleOptions { app?: string; separator?: string }   // default separator ' — '
```

`document.title` follows the frontmost window — `Rides — Garage` — and is the app's name alone with nothing
open. `app` defaults to the document's own title (the page's `<title>`), and is restored on unmount. The
window's name is a string here, not the `ReactNode` `<Desktop title>` renders.

### Commands (the responder chain)

```ts
perform(desk, command: string, args?, options?: ChainOptions): boolean      // true if something handled it
canPerform(desk, command: string, options?: ChainOptions): boolean          // what a menu asks
addCommandHandler(element: EventTarget, command, handler, { enabled? }): () => void
addDeskCommands(stage: EventTarget, desk): () => void
chainStart(desk, options?): EventTarget
windowElement(doc, id): Element | null
DeskCommands = { closeWindow, minimizeWindow, zoomWindow, arrange, nextWindow, previousWindow }
// arrange is answered by a mounted Desktop: 1 fills, 2 split, 3 one tall + two stacked, 4+ a grid of usable cells;
// the focused window takes the first place. Put it in the Window menu as "Arrange", shortcut 'mod+alt+a'.
WINDOW_ATTRIBUTE = 'data-desk-window'; STAGE_ATTRIBUTE = 'data-desk-stage'
```

The chain is the DOM: focused element → its window → stage → document. The first responder that implements
a command decides; if it is disabled the command stops there (AppKit's rule). Events are `desk:perform` and
`desk:can-perform`, bubbling and composed.

### Shortcuts

```ts
bindShortcuts(desk, keymap: Record<string, string>, { target?, apple? }): () => void
parseShortcut('mod+shift+z'): Shortcut
matchesShortcut(event, shortcut, apple?): boolean
formatShortcut('mod+comma', apple?): string        // '⌘,' or 'Ctrl+,'
isApplePlatform(): boolean                         // the KEYBOARD; the look is separate
deviceLook(): Look                                 // 'mac' | 'gnome' | 'windows' for this device
lookFor(platform, userAgent): Look                 // the same, pure; resolveLook('auto' | Look): Look
isInstalledApp(): boolean                          // gate ⌘W / ⌘` on this; never take ⌘T or ⌘N
titleCase('ride card'): string                    // 'Ride Card' — app and window names; a document keeps its own name
isTitleCase(name): boolean                         // for a test over the names an app defines
```

`mod` is ⌘ on Apple, Ctrl elsewhere. Matching also falls back to the physical key, so ⌥] works on a Mac. A
shortcut nothing handles leaves the browser's default alone. Bare keys are ignored while typing in a field.

### Dragging between windows

```tsx
useDragSource<T>({ type, disabled? }): { dragProps(payload, preview?), dragging }   // lists
useDraggable<T>({ type, payload, preview?, disabled? }): { dragProps, dragging }    // one thing
useDropTarget<T>({ accepts, onDrop, disabled? }): { dropProps, over, ready }
useDragging(): Drag | null
interface Drag<T> { type: string; payload: T; from: string | null }
type Accepts = string | string[] | ((type: string) => boolean)
```

Pointer Events, so touch and pen work; Escape calls a drag off; the drop brings the receiving window
forward. `dropProps` carries `data-ready` and `data-over`, which the stylesheet already draws. A
`DeskProvider` supplies the drag state, as it does the bus.

### Events between windows

```ts
createBus(): Bus
interface Bus {
  publish<T>(topic: string, payload: T, options?: { from?: string | null }): DeskEvent<T>
  subscribe<T>(topic: string, handler: (e: DeskEvent<T>) => void, options?: { replay?: boolean }): () => void
  last<T>(topic: string): DeskEvent<T> | undefined
}
interface DeskEvent<T> { topic: string; payload: T; from: string | null; at: number }
topicMatches(pattern, topic): boolean              // 'ride.*' and '*' are the only wildcards
InputCommands = { submit: 'desk.input.submit', describe: 'desk.input.describe' }
```

### Services

Something the desk keeps going that is not a window: a value anything can read and, optionally, a
process that keeps it true. For a dock count on a window that is shut, or data a window should not
wait for when it opens.

```ts
createService<T>({ id, initial, run? }): Service<T>
interface Service<T> {
  id: string
  now(): T
  set(next: T): void                                 // tells readers only when the value is new
  subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void
  hold(): () => void                                 // counted; the release may be called twice
  running(): boolean                                 // true while anything holds it
}
run({ now, set, live }): (() => void) | void         // started on the first hold; the return runs on the last release
holdAll(services): () => void
```

A service does not fetch, cache or retry: `run` brings its own way of getting data. Check `live()`
after every await. A stopped service keeps its value unless `run`'s cleanup sets it back.

### Attention

Whether somebody is looking at a window now, for a service that counts what arrived unseen.

```ts
attentionOn(desk, id, counted = true): Attention     // { counted, front, visible, focused }
attended(a): boolean                                 // front && visible && focused
becomesNews(a): boolean                              // counted && !attended(a)
watchAttention(desk, id, onAttended): () => void     // at once if attended, then on desk change, tab shown, browser focused
```

## React: `@liberation-data/desk/react`

### Shell

```tsx
<DeskShell desk?={Desk} options?={DeskOptions} bus?={Bus} toasts?={true} look?={'auto'} services?={Service[]}>
<DeskProvider desk={desk} look?={'auto'} services?={Service[]}>  // or options={…} to make one
useDesk(): Desk
useLook(): 'mac' | 'gnome' | 'windows'              // resolved; the device's outside a desk
useDeskState(): DeskState
useWindowId(): string | null                        // inside a window's content
useWindowProgress({ value, max, label } | null): boolean  // a real count in this window's title bar; false outside one
useWindowNote(note: ReactNode): boolean             // this view's note in place of the window's; null defers, false hides
useWindowInfo(info: ReactNode): boolean             // this view's (i) in place of the window's; null defers

<Desktop
  renderWindow={(id) => ReactNode}                  // memoised: chrome re-renders, content does not
  title={(id) => ReactNode}
  note?={(id) => ReactNode}                         // quiet text in the title bar: what this window is looking at
  info?={(id) => ReactNode}                         // an (i) at the end of the title bar (start on gnome/windows): what this window IS
  limits?={(id) => ({ maxWidth?, maxHeight?, minWidth?, minHeight? } | null)}  // a window with a natural
                                                    // size is never stretched past it; filled, it centres
  actions?={(id) => ReactNode}                      // window-wide controls in the title bar
  loading?={(id) => ReactNode}                      // inside a window while its code loads
  failed?={(id, error, reload) => ReactNode}        // inside a window that could not open
  empty?={ReactNode}
  layout?={'auto' | 'desktop' | 'fullscreen'}       // auto: touch screens get one window at a time
  className?={string}
/>
```

### Loading and failing, per window

```tsx
const RoutePlanner = lazyWindow(() => import('./apps/RoutePlanner'))   // use in renderWindow
```

The default fallback is `<Loading label="Loading" />`; pass `loading` to `Desktop` to replace it.
Every window has its own Suspense and error boundary: one window loading or throwing never blanks another,
the menu bar or the dock. A failure is logged with `console.error` and shows Reload, which remounts the
window; `lazyWindow` retries its import on reload, unlike `React.lazy`, which caches a failed import.

### Inside a window

```tsx
<Pane label?={string} header?={ReactNode} footer?={ReactNode} bodyRef?={Ref} onScroll?={fn}>{scrolling content}</Pane>
<Pane padded …>   // 16px clear edge, children spaced by gap: for a page of content, not a table or a log
<PaneHeader title={ReactNode} actions?={ReactNode} />   // the pane's title and its Refresh, on one row
<Section title={ReactNode} actions?={ReactNode}>{content}</Section>   // a titled group inside a pane
<Toolbar label?={string} trailing?={ReactNode}>{controls}</Toolbar>   // className="desk-grow" takes spare room
<Page label?={string} fill?>{long text}</Page>   // a sheet for text read at length, on --desk-page; fill = at least the room's height
// --desk-page-tint (4% light, 5% dark) is how much --desk-accent is mixed into the page; 0% for the neutral alone.
// text size by class, never px: desk-text-body | desk-text-small | desk-text-caption, plus desk-text-muted.
// the scale is tokens: --desk-text-caption 11, -small 12, -body 13, -lead 15, -title 17, -display 22, -hero 28.
<InfoTip label={string} placement?={'below'|'above'} align?={'start'|'end'}>{explanation}</InfoTip>
// the (i) wears --desk-info (the title bar's green) so it is seen; retint it there, not in the selector.
```

A pane fills its window and scrolls only its middle, so the window never scrolls and the toolbar stays put.
A named pane is a focusable region, so it scrolls from the keyboard. InfoTip is an (i) popover for
explanation only — never a warning, which belongs in front of people.

### Dock

```tsx
<Dock entries={DockEntry[]} label?="Dock" placement?={'overlay' | 'inline'} side?={'left' | 'right' | 'bottom'}
  pins?={{ accepts, onPin: (drag, before: id | null) => void, onMove?: (id, before: id | null) => void }} />
dockItem({ id, label, icon, window?, description?, badge?, onSelect?, disabled?, contextMenu?: () => MenuItem[], movable? })
dockStack({ id, label, items: DockItem[], icon?, contextMenu?: () => MenuItem[], movable? })
dockSeparator(id)
```

An item opens `window ?? id` and shows a dot while that window is open, accent when it is key. `side`
defaults to `left`. A stack fans out toward the desk. One tab stop; arrow keys along it (Up/Down at a side,
Left/Right at the bottom); Escape folds a stack away.
Pins: the app stores kept items and passes them back as entries. A drop on the dock keeps at the end; on a
`movable` item or stack, in front of it. Movable items and stacks drag along the dock (type DOCK_ITEM, payload id).

### Menu bar

```tsx
<MenuBar menus={Menu[]} status?={Menu[]} leading?={ReactNode} trailing?={ReactNode} shortcuts?={true} />
interface Menu { id: string; label: string; title?: ReactNode; emphasis?: boolean; items: MenuItem[] | (() => MenuItem[]) }
// emphasis: the app's own menu, its name in bold, conventionally first
menuCommand(label, command, { shortcut?, checked?, detail?, args? })
menuAction(label, onSelect, { disabled?, shortcut?, checked?, detail? })
menuSeparator(); menuHeader(label)
windowMenuItems(state, focus, title): MenuItem[]

const { target, menu, open } = useContextMenu({ label, items: () => MenuItem[], disabled? })
// spread `target` (onContextMenu, onKeyDown) on the element; render `menu` anywhere (portal).
// Right-click opens at the pointer; Menu key / Shift+F10 at the element. Commands run from that element.

<IconView label items={{id, label, icon, subtitle?, badge?, disabled?, draggable?}[]} onOpen={item => …}
  openOn?="double"|"single" selected? onSelectionChange? contextMenu?={item => MenuItem[]}
  drag?={{ type, payload: item => unknown }} empty? className? />
// click selects, double-click / Return opens (single: click opens); arrows, Home/End, type-ahead. Needs a DeskProvider.
```

Command items are enabled via `canPerform` as the menu opens, and menus bind their own shortcuts. Opening a
menu does not take focus from the key window, so a chosen command reaches the same responder a shortcut
would. `items` as a function is re-read on every open.

### Commands and input

```tsx
useCommand<Args>(command, handler, { enabled?: boolean | (() => boolean), at?: 'window' | 'app' | RefObject })
usePerform(): (command, args?) => boolean
useCanPerform(): (command) => boolean
useShortcuts(keymap, { target?, apple? })

useWindowInput(handler: (text: string) => void, { placeholder?, target?, disabled? })
<InputBar onSubmit={(text) => void} fallbackPlaceholder? fallbackTarget? label?
          mode?={'summoned' | 'inline'} shortcut?={'mod+j' | null} />   // summoned: centred, Escape closes
InputCommands.open = 'desk.input.open'                                   // a menu item can summon it
```

`useCommand` defaults to the window it is rendered in, and to the app outside one.

### Dragging between windows

```tsx
useDragSource<T>({ type, disabled? }): { dragProps(payload, preview?), dragging }   // lists
useDraggable<T>({ type, payload, preview?, disabled? }): { dragProps, dragging }    // one thing
useDropTarget<T>({ accepts, onDrop, disabled? }): { dropProps, over, ready }
useDragging(): Drag | null
interface Drag<T> { type: string; payload: T; from: string | null }
type Accepts = string | string[] | ((type: string) => boolean)
```

Pointer Events, so touch and pen work; Escape calls a drag off; the drop brings the receiving window
forward. `dropProps` carries `data-ready` and `data-over`, which the stylesheet already draws. A
`DeskProvider` supplies the drag state, as it does the bus.

### Events

```tsx
<BusProvider bus?={Bus}>                              // optional: a desk already carries a bus
useBus(): Bus
usePublish(): <T>(topic, payload) => DeskEvent<T>     // stamped with the window it came from
useDeskEvent<T>(topic, handler, { replay? })          // replay: deliver the last event immediately
```

### Services

```tsx
<DeskShell services={[rides, unread]}>                // held from mount to unmount; the array is read once
useService(service): T                               // the value, live, and the service held while mounted
useServiceValue(service): T                          // the value, live, without holding: for a badge
```

### Generated apps

```tsx
<AppFrame title src?|srcDoc? listens?={string[]} says?={string[]} accepts?={Accepts} opens?={string[]}
          theme?={{ mode: 'light'|'dark', tokens: Record<string,string> }}
          sandbox?="allow-scripts allow-forms" />
// theme: sent with hello and again on change; the bridge sets the tokens as custom properties on the
// app's root, with data-theme and color-scheme (the attribute desk's own CSS and the HIG use). The app may read desk.theme / desk.onTheme(fn).
withAppBridge(html): string          // puts the app-side script in the page's <head>
APP_BRIDGE_SCRIPT                    // the same script, to include some other way
```

Inside the page: `desk.on(topic, message => …)`, `desk.onDrop(message => …)`, `desk.publish(topic, payload)`,
`desk.open(window)`, `desk.theme`, `desk.onTheme(fn)`, and `desk.window` once connected. Messages carry `desk: 1`. The host ignores anything not
from its own frame, drops publishes outside `says` and opens outside `opens`, never echoes an app its own
events, and sets the frame's `pointer-events: none` while a drag is in the air so drops reach it.

### Search

```tsx
<SearchPalette open onOpenChange search={(q) => SearchResult[] | Promise<SearchResult[]>}
               placeholder? label? hint? empty?={(q) => ReactNode} shortcut?={'mod+k' | null} />
interface SearchResult { id; title; subtitle?; group?; icon?; kind?; onSelect(): void }
windowResults(desk, title, group?): SearchResult[]
SearchCommand = 'desk.search'                          // a menu item can open it
```

### Controls

```tsx
<Button intent?={'normal'|'default'|'quiet'|'destructive'} size?={'regular'|'small'} icon? … />
<SegmentedControl options={{value,label,icon?,disabled?}[]} value onChange label size? disabled? width?={fit|fill} />
                                                  // selection is one sliding `.desk-segment-thumb`, not a fill on the option;
                                                  // on dark it is the surface lightened and tinted 14% with the accent;
                                                  // --desk-segment-thumb replaces its fill
                                                  // track is 32px tall (26 small), 4 more than a button
<Tabs tabs={{value,label,badge?,disabled?}[]} value onChange label actions?>{selected view}</Tabs>
                                                  // switches the view below; a segmented control chooses
<Toggle checked onChange label? description? disabled? aria-label? />        // applies at once
<Checkbox checked indeterminate? onChange label? description? disabled? />   // waits for Save
<Slider value onChange label min? max? step? disabled? format?={(v) => string} />
<TextField label labelHidden? help? error? … />                             // error marks it invalid
<RadioGroup options={{value,label,description?,disabled?}[]} value onChange label labelHidden? />
<ChoiceGroup options={{value,label,description?,icon?,tag?,disabled?}[]} value onChange label labelHidden? />
                                                  // cards for a setup step; native radios, arrow keys move the choice
<PopUpButton value={T|null} onChange options={{value,label,description?,icon?,disabled?}[]}
             label labelHidden? placeholder? disabled? size? />
<Disclosure label open onOpenChange summary?={ReactNode} className?>{folded controls}</Disclosure>
                                                  // one caret button; summary sits beside it folded or open;
                                                  // the body stays mounted while folded, so fields keep their values
<Chip onRemove? removeLabel? className?>{a word or two}</Chip>               // one thing set or chosen; × only with onRemove
```

### Waiting

```tsx
<Spinner label size?={'small'|'regular'|'large'} showLabel?={false} />   // inline; label is read, not shown
<Loading label slow?={ReactNode} slowAfterMs?={3000} size?={'large'} />  // a view with nothing on it yet
```

### Status lamps

```tsx
<Led color={'off'|'green'|'amber'|'red'} label? />   // label read aloud; omit it when words sit beside the lamp
```

The colour is named for what it looks like; what it means is the app's to say, in words too — a lamp is
never the only thing carrying a state. Its colours are `--desk-led-*`, bright on both grounds, not the
`--desk-ok`/`--desk-warn`/`--desk-bad` text tokens, which are dark on a light ground and look switched off.

### Page dots

```tsx
<PageDots count value label={'Tip'} max?={7} className? />   // value from 0; read aloud as "Tip 3 of 9"
pageWindow(count, value, max?): { index, size: 'full'|'medium'|'small' }[]   // the dots it draws
```

Position in a short run of pages. Past `max` it draws a window around the current dot and shrinks the dots
at an edge with more beyond it, so the row never grows. It is `role="img"` and takes no focus: a button
beside it moves between pages. Fewer than two pages draws nothing.

Both are one `role="status"`. `Loading` shows `slow` once the wait passes `slowAfterMs`, inside that same
region, so its arrival is the announcement; the timer restarts when `slow` or `slowAfterMs` changes. There
is no determinate bar: a bar needs a fraction the browser can see, and work with real steps is a
`Checklist`. `Loading` fills the height it is given, so give its parent one.

### Lists

```tsx
<Table rows columns rowId={(row) => string} label rowProps?={(row) => object}
       selected?={string | string[] | null} selection?={'single' | 'multiple'}
       onSelect? onSelectionChange? onActivate? sort? onSortChange? empty? />
interface Column<Row> { key; header; render?; align?; numeric?; sortable?; width? }
interface Sort { key: string; direction: 'ascending' | 'descending' }

<Sidebar sections={{ id, label?, items: { id, label, icon?, badge?, disabled? }[] }[]}
         value onChange label footer? />

<Outline rows={{ id, label, depth, disabled? }[]} value={string | null} onChange showing? label />
```

Outline: a hierarchy as a flat list in reading order, each row saying its `depth` (1 is the top). Use it
for a document's headings, a schema, a folder — not `Sidebar`, which is a few places at one level. One tab
stop; up and down move through the rows, left goes out to the parent and right in to the first child, Home
and End to the ends. Depth is drawn with weight, colour and indent, and stops changing at the fourth level
(`OUTLINE_MAX_DEPTH`). A `disabled` row is listed and cannot be chosen. `showing` names the rows on show
along with `value` (a page that holds several headings): they are marked as the chosen row is, and
`value` stays where the keyboard is. Marked rows that touch are drawn as one block, a `disabled` row
among them included.

Table: one tab stop, arrow keys move the selection, Enter or double click activates, `aria-sort` on
sortable headings. It renders what it is given — no paging, no fetching.

### Overlays

```tsx
<Popover open onOpenChange label trigger={(props) => <Button {...props} />} placement? align? />  // floats over its window, clamped to it; never resizes it
<Sheet open onDismiss title description? actions? />        // renders inside its own window
<Alert open title message? confirmLabel onConfirm onCancel cancelLabel? destructive? />
<ToastProvider>; useToast(): { show(toast): string; dismiss(id): void }
toast.show({ message, tone?: 'neutral'|'ok'|'bad', action?: { label, onSelect }, duration?: 6000 })
```

All share one layer stack: Escape dismisses the topmost. Popover, Sheet and Alert trap focus and return it.
A toast pauses while the pointer or focus is on it.

### Conversation

```tsx
<Thread messages={Message[]} me?="me" typing? onRetry? empty? label? />
interface Message { id; from; authorName?; body: ReactNode; at?: Date | string; state?: 'sending'|'sent'|'failed' }
<Composer value onChange onSubmit placeholder? label? disabled? busy? onStop? accessory? maxRows? />
```

No transport of its own. The thread follows new messages only while the reader is at the end. The composer
sends on Enter, keeps Shift+Enter for a new line, and never sends mid-composition in an input method.

### Teaching and first run

```tsx
<TourBar tour={{ id, name, description?, steps }} onFinish? onStop? offer? />
interface TourStep { window?: string; point?: string; caption: ReactNode; yourTurn?: boolean;
                   until?: string | { topic: string; when: (event: DeskEvent) => boolean } }

const tasks = useTasks(Task[]): { items: TaskProgress[]; running; done; failed; start(); restart() }
interface Task { id; name: ReactNode; detail?: ReactNode; run: (report: (detail: ReactNode) => void) => unknown }
<Checklist items={TaskProgress[]} onRetry? progress?={true} label? />   // a failed row shows its error and Try again

const setup = useSetupProgress({ key, initial: Answers, store?: SetupStore })
  // { loaded, index, setIndex, answers, answer(patch), finished, finish(), reset() }
interface SetupStore<A> { load(): SetupRecord<A> | undefined | Promise<…>; save(record): void | Promise<void>; clear() }
localSetupStore(key)   // the default: localStorage under `desk.setup.<key>`; never put secrets in answers

<Wizard steps={WizardStep[]} index onIndexChange onFinish label? />
interface WizardStep { id; name; title; description?; body?; glyph?; complete?; continueLabel?;
                       skip?: { label, onSkip }; working?; onEnter?;
                       onContinue?: () => unknown | Promise<unknown>; busyLabel? }
```

A tour step opens its window and points at `point` (a `data-tour` name or a selector). A step with `until` moves on
when that event is published (no Done button). `offer` shows the tour's name and description with Show me / Not now
(Not now calls onStop) and opens nothing until accepted — use it right after setup. A wizard step offers
Continue only when `complete`, and `working` steps offer no Back. `onContinue` runs before moving on: Continue
shows `busyLabel` (default "Working…") and is disabled; a thrown Error's message is shown in the step and the
step stays; returning `false` stays silently. Pressing again while it runs does nothing. Return performs Continue from a
field or the step heading (same gating); a focused button, link, select or textarea keeps it. Tasks run in order and
stop at the first that throws; `start()` runs whatever is not done (the retry), `restart()` runs them all again.
For a waiting step: `working: !tasks.failed, complete: tasks.done, onEnter: tasks.restart`.

## Styling

Every value reads a `--desk-*` token; redefine tokens, never override selectors. Colour roles: `--desk-ground`,
`--desk-surface`, `--desk-titlebar`, `--desk-ink`, `--desk-muted`, `--desk-rule`, `--desk-accent`,
`--desk-ok|warn|bad`, `--desk-on-accent`. Spacing `--desk-space-1..7` = 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48 px. Also
`--desk-radius`, `--desk-control-height`, `--desk-control-radius`, `--desk-font`, `--desk-font-mono`,
`--desk-ease`, `--desk-dock-size`, `--desk-dock-glass`, `--desk-dock-offset`, `--desk-dock-room`,
`--desk-inset-bottom`, `--desk-wizard-height`, `--desk-field-gap`.

Light and dark follow `prefers-color-scheme`; `data-theme="light" | "dark"` on the root wins. The look is
`data-look="mac" | "gnome" | "windows"` on the root, set by the desk; don't set it yourself — pass `look`.

## Sounds: `@liberation-data/desk/fx`

```ts
const fx = createFx({ storageKey?: 'app.sounds-muted', coalesceMs?: 1500, volume?: 0.8,
                      sounds?: { chime: (ctx, out, at) => void } })   // one per app, module scope
fx.unlock()                         // once, at startup: opens audio on the first press
fx.play('attention' | 'ready' | 'failed' | <own>)   // → boolean; silent if muted, repeated, or before a press
fx.muted(); fx.setMuted(bool); fx.subscribe(() => …)                   // follows other tabs too
await measureLoudness(fx, 'failed', { speaker: 'laptop' })            // → { lufs, peakDb }; browser only
<SoundsToggle fx={fx} label? description? />                          // from /react: the one switch
```

`attention`: something is waiting on this person. `ready`: something to look at when they are ready.
`failed`: their work did not finish. Each is matched to -27 LUFS on a laptop speaker. `scored(score)`
builds a sound in the same family from a `Score` (`BELL` and `GROWL` are the voices). When to play one
is the app's decision: HIG §7, Sound.

## Testing

```ts
const desk = createDesk({ stage: () => ({ width: 1000, height: 700 }) })   // jsdom measures nothing
render(<DeskProvider desk={desk}>…</DeskProvider>)
```

Query a window by `[data-desk-window="id"]`: on a touch layout an offstage window is `inert`, so it is not
in the accessibility tree.

## Facts an agent should not guess

- React 19 is a peer dependency; the core entry point imports no React and touches no DOM except through
  the command helpers and `attentionOn`/`watchAttention`, which read the page when there is one.
- A service runs only while held. Give it to the desk (`services`) or read it with `useService`; a
  service nobody holds never starts its `run`. `useServiceValue` does not hold.
- Focus follows the key window when it changes, but never on first render.
- First run (HIG §8): check on Continue with `onContinue`, not on the next step; show waiting work with
  `useTasks` + `Checklist`; open the chosen window last so it is in front; offer the tour (`offer`) once on
  arrival; remember progress with `useSetupProgress`, and never put passwords or keys in its answers.
- A `DeskProvider` already carries an event bus; `BusProvider` is only for supplying or sharing one.
- `renderWindow` must be stable (module scope or `useCallback`) for the memoisation to hold.
- `parse`/`syncWithLocation` warn once when no `isKnown` is given: unknown ids from a URL are then trusted.
- `npm run size` enforces a gzipped budget: core 16 KiB, react 62 KiB, css 20 KiB, fx 5 KiB.
- `fx.play` never resumes audio itself: outside a press a browser's resume may never settle. Call
  `fx.unlock()` at startup, or nothing sounds until a press after the sound was due.
- The package is ESM only, with `"sideEffects": ["**/*.css"]`.
